transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I don’t feel any interest in the things I used to love—my art, my garden, even time with my family just feels flat. I just can't seem to find the joy in any of it anymore, and everything just feels completely gray.

Have you had other separate periods in your life lasting at least two weeks when you felt this same loss of interest or depression, with times in between when you felt mostly back to normal? Or has this low mood been more or less continuous for years?

No, it hasn't been continuous; these heavy, empty stretches have come and gone over the last two years, totaling about seven months. In between, there are times when my mood feels completely neutral, and other separate periods where I actually feel very sped-up and high-energy.

During your depressive episodes, have you ever had psychotic symptoms, like hearing or seeing things others couldn’t, or being firmly convinced of something that others said wasn’t true? If yes, did those happen only when you were severely depressed?

Yes, I do hear whispering voices sometimes and get this strong feeling that my family is secretly testing me, but it doesn't only happen when I'm depressed. I've actually experienced those things when I was feeling very wired and high-energy, and even during a stretch last year when my mood felt completely neutral.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent mood episodes over two years, including depressive episodes with marked anhedonia and distinct periods of elevated/high-energy mood, consistent with bipolar disorder. Psychotic symptoms are confirmed and are not restricted to depressive episodes, occurring during high-energy states and even during a euthymic/neutral period. Given the provided candidate set, the best-fitting diagnosis is bipolar affective disorder with psychotic symptoms.
